description: Job Title: Quality Assurance Analyst Job Description The Quality Assurance Analyst is a crucial role responsible for upholding the highest standards of product quality and ensuring compliance with industry regulations and company policies. The analyst will play a key part in maintaining compliance with GMP, SQF, HACCP, FDA, and State regulations through various auditing and testing methods. Responsibilities Ensure compliance with industry standards and regulations, including GMP, SQF, HACCP, FDA, and State requirements. Conduct audits, mock recalls, self-inspections, and verify Certificates of Analysis (COAs). Perform microbiological testing and uphold food safety protocols. Collaborate with operations, sanitation, and maintenance teams to drive continuous improvement initiatives. Conduct case audits and participate in root cause analysis and quality documentation. Monitor critical control points and participate in batch record reviews and environmental monitoring. Essential Skills Proficiency in quality assurance and quality control practices. Strong knowledge of GMP, HACCP, and food safety protocols. Experience with inspections, quality analysis, and documentation. Understanding of FDA regulations and compliance. Ability to conduct microbiological testing and environmental monitoring. Additional Skills & Qualifications 1-5 years of experience with a Degree in the Sciences, or 5+ years of experience in Quality within a GMP/FDA facility. Strong experience in biology and understanding of critical control points. Work Environment This position operates Monday through Friday, with potential for overtime and weekend work as needed. The role is part of a rotation schedule, requiring flexibility for audits or food safety emergencies. The work environment demands a commitment to extra hours when necessary to ensure compliance and quality assurance Job Type & Location This is a Permanent position based out of Oak Creek, WI. Pay and Benefits The pay range for this position is $68000.00 - $83000.00/yr. Individual compensation offered for this position within this range will depend on many factors, including qualifications, skills, relevant experience, job knowledge, geographic location, internal equity, and other pertinent job-related factors. This is a direct placement position. Any benefits will be provided upon start of assignment or earlier if requested by client. Workplace Type This is a fully onsite position in Oak Creek,WI. Clinical Lab Analyst (Overnight Shift) Job Description Responsibilities Perform newborn screening testing on blood spot specimens using immunoassay, enzyme assay, electrophoresis, high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), tandem mass spectrometry, and molecular methods. Operate, monitor, and perform daily operation and routine maintenance on laboratory instruments and equipment in accordance with established procedures. Perform calibration of laboratory instruments and assist in troubleshooting instrument and method performance issues. Document and review newborn screening test data, procedures, and results with a high level of accuracy and attention to detail. Release test data and reports for use by physicians, health care professionals, and newborn screening medical follow-up teams, ensuring timeliness and accuracy. Develop and maintain standard operating procedures and assist in preparing documentation for test verification and validation studies. Perform quality control and quality assurance procedures in accordance with established standard operating procedures and policies. Recognize basic problems in laboratory methods and performance, document issues, and assist in troubleshooting to resolve them. Assemble and organize quality control data for further analysis, recognize trends or problems, and participate in root cause analysis. Initiate and document corrective actions in response to identified quality issues and contribute to continuous improvement of laboratory processes. Rotate through three separate testing areas, performing assigned testing in one area per shift and moving to a different area on subsequent shifts. Follow all laboratory safety procedures and regulatory requirements while handling specimens, reagents, and equipment. Collaborate with a small overnight team to ensure continuous coverage and timely completion of newborn screening tests. Use downtime productively by engaging in additional training, cross-training in different testing areas, and enhancing technical knowledge. Essential Skills Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Genetics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Eligibility under Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) qualifications for high complexity testing, including at least 6 semesters of Biology and 6 semesters of Chemistry. At least 3 months of hands-on laboratory experience, which may include work performed in a laboratory setting during school, beyond standard coursework-only lab classes. Strong foundational knowledge in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, and Genetics. Experience working in a laboratory environment, including handling biological specimens and using standard laboratory equipment. Ability to perform and interpret quality control and quality assurance procedures in alignment with laboratory policies. Job Description Clinical Lab Analyst (Overnight Shift) This is a great opportunity to join a high-complexity clinical laboratory that plays a critical role in newborn screening programs. In this position, you'll work with advanced laboratory technologies to help identify potentially life-threatening conditions in newborns, directly supporting positive patient outcomes. You'll perform testing on newborn blood spot specimens using a variety of techniques including immunoassay, enzyme assays, electrophoresis, HPLC, tandem mass spectrometry, and molecular methods. Responsibilities include operating and maintaining laboratory instrumentation, reviewing and documenting test results, performing quality control procedures, troubleshooting equipment and assay issues, and ensuring accurate, timely reporting of results. The lab operates 24/7, providing excellent hands-on experience with sophisticated instrumentation and high-throughput testing workflows. Analysts rotate through multiple testing areas, offering broad technical exposure and opportunities to expand their skill set through ongoing training and cross-training. What makes this role stand out: Hands-on experience with advanced clinical laboratory technologies Opportunity to support meaningful newborn screening programs Strong focus on quality assurance, data analysis, and continuous improvement Exposure to molecular testing, mass spectrometry, HPLC, and other specialized methodologies Collaborative team environment with extensive learning and growth opportunities Schedule: Overnight shift: 9:30 PM to 7:30 AM Rotating 5 days on, 4 days off schedule Includes weekends and holidays Initial training is typically completed on a daytime schedule before transitioning to nights This role is ideal for candidates with a Biology, Chemistry, Biochemistry, Genetics, or related scientific background who are looking to build a career in clinical laboratory science and gain experience working in a regulated, high-complexity testing environment. Job Type & Location This is a Contract to Hire position based out of Ankeny, IA. Pay and Benefits The pay range for this position is $20.00 - $20.00/hr. Job Title: GIS Analyst Job Description Join our team in supporting the Enhanced Alternative Connect America Model (E-ACAM) fiber work, focusing on the deployment of fiber optic networks in rural areas. This program, backed by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), aims to bring high-speed broadband to remote locations through financial assistance to telecommunications carriers. Responsibilities Analyze and transform ROW/fiber route data into usable information. Extract fiber paths from ARC GIS-based web software for engineering purposes. Provide data for construction drawings and permit packages. Update fiber paths and permit polygons within the GIS software. Create and maintain reports, documentation, and data standards. Manage multiple projects and work queues while meeting deadlines. Essential Skills Minimum of 1-3 years experience using ARC Pro or equivalent GIS proficiency. Strong GIS and data analysis skills. Analytical problem-solving abilities. Experience with telecom design, although CAD/designer work is minimal. Experience analyzing and transforming ROW/fiber route data. Ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines. Strong attention to detail and ability to work independently. Effective written and verbal communication skills. Experience in cross-functional collaboration. Additional Skills & Qualifications Experience in telecommunications, ROW, permitting, or fiber infrastructure is preferred. Work Environment This is a 100% remote position on a team of 6 coordinators and 2 leads dedicated to the project. The role requires working a 40-hour work week with core hours from 9 AM to 3 PM CST. Flexibility is allowed outside of these hours as long as daily deadlines are met. The necessary hardware, including a computer, desktop, keypad, and mouse, will be provided. Job Type & Location This is a Contract position based out of Madison, WI. Pay and Benefits The pay range for this position is $25.00 - $30.00/hr. Job Title: GIS Analyst Job Description The GIS Analyst will support Operation Services, an internal department that aids construction projects. The role involves completing engineering designs and cost estimates using GIS for various main and service works, collecting construction activity 'as-built' data with mobile CPS devices in the field, creating permanent asset records, and editing map features and correlating attribute data in GIS. The analyst will also perform final quality checks on GIS versioned data before posting, represent Engineering at project meetings, and conduct field visits to job sites to determine requirements for service and main work. Responsibilities Complete engineering designs and cost estimates using GIS for all types of main and service work. Collect construction activity 'as-built' using mobile CPS devices in the field for creating permanent asset records. Edit map features and correlating attribute data in the GIS. Perform final quality checks on GIS versioned data before it is posted to the GIS. Represent Engineering at internal and external project meetings as required. Visit job sites to determine requirements for service and main work. Perform preliminary reviews of development plans and interface with customers. Implement and train Engineering staff on new work processes for the GIS mapping system. Distribute and update maps for other departments as requested. Approve requests for the acquisition and release of easements and vacation of rights-of-way. Perform pipeline safety compliance-related GIS analysis as directed. Execute all other duties as assigned. Essential Skills Proficiency in ArcGIS and CAD. Knowledge of geography and construction drawings. Experience with as-built drawings, cost forecasting, and drafting. Additional Skills & Qualifications Ability to complete engineering designs and cost estimates using GIS. Experience in collecting construction activity 'as-built' data using mobile CPS devices. Skill in editing map features and correlating attribute data in GIS. Work Environment The role is based in a professional engineering office, initially requiring attendance five days per week, reducing to three days per week after training. Work may be performed in both office and field settings, with exposure to the elements. Typical hours are 7:00 a.m. to 3:45 p.m., Monday through Friday, with potential for overtime and travel. Microbiology Lab Analyst Job Description The Microbiology Lab Analyst serves as a Laboratory Technician responsible for performing analytical and microbiological testing on food products, ingredients, and environmental samples to support quality and safety programs. You will apply approved microbiological techniques and methodologies to ensure accurate, reliable results and help maintain compliance with regulatory and customer requirements. Working primarily on second shift, you will prepare and analyze samples, maintain a clean and organized laboratory, monitor and care for equipment, and assist with inventory and quality-related duties. Responsibilities Perform analytical and microbiological testing of food products, ingredients, and environmental samples in accordance with approved methods and protocols. Apply approved microbiological techniques and methodologies to evaluate indicator organisms, pathogens, and relevant chemistries. Prepare and analyze samples for indicator organisms, pathogens, and chemical parameters, ensuring accuracy and proper documentation. Notify laboratory management promptly of any deviations, out-of-specification results, or unusual findings in test results. Maintain appropriate inventory levels of reagents, media, consumables, and supplies required for testing activities. Provide routine preventive maintenance, basic troubleshooting, and thorough cleaning of laboratory equipment to ensure reliable operation. Support quality-related duties, including performing temperature checks, monitoring controls, and verifying proper storage conditions. Adhere to company policies, procedures, and customer requirements while following relevant regulatory and industry guidelines. Maintain a clean, organized, and safe laboratory environment using proper aseptic techniques and good laboratory practices. Stay current with scientific literature, emerging technologies, and industry trends related to food microbiology and analytical testing. Accurately record, interpret, and report test results in accordance with laboratory documentation standards. Collaborate with colleagues and other departments to support continuous improvement in laboratory processes and quality systems. Essential Skills Bachelor's degree in biology, chemistry, or a closely related science field. At least 2 years of experience in a commercial food-testing or analytical laboratory. Hands-on experience with microbiological testing of food products, ingredients, or environmental samples. Proficiency in aseptic sampling techniques and routine laboratory procedures. Knowledge of laboratory equipment operation, care, and basic troubleshooting. Familiarity with Good Laboratory Practices (GLP). Working knowledge of OSHA safety requirements in a laboratory environment. Experience with FDA, BAM, APHA, ISO, or USP methods relevant to microbiology or analytical testing. Ability to follow detailed protocols and standard operating procedures accurately. Strong attention to detail

Job Title: Molecular Lab Analyst Job Description The Molecular Lab Analyst (Laboratory Analyst II) performs general sample preparation, DNA extractions, and routine PCR and qPCR testing to support GMO analysis of agricultural and food products. This role focuses on executing established testing methods, analyzing and documenting results, troubleshooting laboratory processes, supporting quality systems, and maintaining strict compliance with laboratory procedures and regulatory requirements. The position offers the opportunity to contribute to a growing laboratory operation with modern equipment, diverse projects, and a collaborative, family-style team environment, with potential for full-time employment and holiday pay as part of the contract. Responsibilities Perform quantitative and qualitative GMO testing on corn, soy, and processed food products using established PCR and qPCR methods. Prepare samples, including grinding received agricultural and food product samples, and ensure proper handling and labeling throughout the testing process. Prepare reagents, controls, standards, and PCR plates in accordance with laboratory standard operating procedures (SOPs) and quality standards. Set up and execute PCR and qPCR runs, including manual preparation of reactions without kits, following in-house protocols. Use 96-well plates and transfer to 384-well plates accurately, employing multiple types of pipettes to support high-throughput testing. Analyze test results, perform required calculations, and accurately document findings in laboratory information systems and records. Troubleshoot PCR workflows, instrumentation issues, and testing deviations to ensure timely, accurate, and reliable results. Support nonconformance investigations and root cause analysis activities related to laboratory testing, data integrity, and processes. Perform routine maintenance, calibration checks, and minor repairs on laboratory equipment to maintain optimal performance. Execute and document QA/QC activities in accordance with SOPs, quality systems, and applicable regulatory requirements. Assist with SOP revisions and updates to reflect process improvements and current best practices. Support the training of new laboratory staff on procedures, equipment, and quality requirements. Participate in continuous improvement initiatives within the Quality Management System (QMS) to enhance efficiency and quality. Cross-train in mycotoxin testing using LCMS, following established procedures and quality standards. Lift items up to 25 pounds from floor to ceiling as needed during the shift to support sample handling and laboratory operations. Work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced testing environment, adapting to changing sample flow and priorities. Collaborate with colleagues to maintain a service-oriented, team-focused culture and demonstrate the value of the growing laboratory. Essential Skills Bachelor's degree in Biology, Molecular Biology, Microbiology, Bioche

Job Title: Molecular Lab Analyst Job Description The Molecular Lab Analyst (Laboratory Analyst II) performs general sample preparation, DNA extractions, and routine PCR and qPCR testing to support GMO analysis of agricultural and food products. This role focuses on executing established testing methods, analyzing results, troubleshooting laboratory processes, supporting quality systems, and maintaining compliance with laboratory procedures and regulatory requirements. The position offers the opportunity to work with modern equipment in a growing laboratory, contribute to a variety of projects, and potentially transition to a full-time role. Responsibilities Perform quantitative and qualitative GMO testing on corn, soy, and processed food products using established PCR and qPCR methods. Prepare samples, including grinding received grain and food samples, and accurately prepare reagents, controls, standards, and PCR plates in accordance with laboratory SOPs and quality standards. Conduct DNA extractions and molecular assays while maintaining aseptic technique to avoid sample contamination. Use 96-well plates and transfer to 384-well plates, applying precise single-channel, multi-channel, and micro-pipetting techniques. Analyze test results, perform required calculations, and document findings accurately and completely in laboratory systems. Troubleshoot PCR workflows, instrumentation issues, and testing deviations to ensure timely, accurate, and reliable results. Support nonconformance investigations and root cause analysis related to laboratory testing and processes. Perform routine maintenance, calibration checks, and minor repairs on laboratory equipment to ensure proper function and data integrity. Execute and document QA/QC activities in accordance with SOPs, quality systems, and applicable regulatory or accreditation requirements. Assist with revisions to standard operating procedures (SOPs) and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives within the Quality Management System (QMS). Help train new laboratory staff on methods, procedures, and quality practices as needed. Cross-train in mycotoxin testing using LCMS following established procedures. Manage varying sample volumes, typically 10–15 samples during off-season and 30–60 samples during peak harvest seasons, while meeting turnaround time expectations. Work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced testing environment, adjusting workflow and hours as needed based on sample flow and customer requirements. Adhere to all laboratory safety practices and maintain a clean, organized, and compliant work area. Essential Skills Bachelor's degree in Biology, Molecular Biology, Microbiology, Biochemistry, or a closely related scientific discipline. 2–4 years of laboratory experience with hands-on PCR and qPCR testing. Strong pipetting skills, including single-channel, multi-channel, and micro-pipetting, with the ability to work precisely and consistently. Demonstrated experience in DNA

QC Analyst Position Summary We are seeking a detail-oriented QC Analyst to support testing activities in both our Quality Control (QC) Laboratory and Feed Analysis Laboratory. This position is ideal for recent Chemistry graduates, candidates with undergraduate research experience, or early-career laboratory professionals looking to build hands-on experience in a GMP-regulated environment. The QC Analyst will perform wet chemistry testing, sample preparation, analytical testing, and documentation activities while ensuring compliance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and Good Documentation Practices (GDP). Training will be provided on site-specific methods and procedures. What You'll Do Quality Control Laboratory Perform routine wet chemistry and laboratory testing, including sieve analysis, thin layer chromatography (TLC), and loss on drying (LOD). Prepare samples, reagents, and solutions according to established procedures. Conduct testing on raw materials and finished products while maintaining high levels of accuracy and attention to detail. Record testing results and observations in laboratory notebooks and electronic systems in compliance with GMP and GDP requirements. Manage sample preparation and testing workflows to support laboratory throughput goals. Feed Analysis Laboratory Receive, log, and track incoming customer feed samples. Prepare samples for analysis through grinding, weighing, dilution, and solution preparation. Perform analytical testing using methods such as HPLC, UV-Vis spectroscopy, and chromatography techniques. Accurately document test results and communicate findings to laboratory leadership. Support increased testing volumes during peak periods while maintaining quality standards. General Responsibilities Follow established laboratory procedures, testing methods, and safety guidelines. Maintain a clean, organized, and inspection-ready laboratory environment. Collaborate effectively with laboratory team members and cross-functional departments. Learn and apply new laboratory methods, instruments, and workflows as needed. Contribute to a culture of quality, safety, and continuous improvement. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical Biology, or a related scientific discipline. Hands-on laboratory experience gained through coursework, undergraduate research, internships, co-ops, or industry experience. Strong attention to detail and ability to accurately document laboratory data. Comfortable working in a fast-paced laboratory environment with multiple priorities. Strong communication, organization, and teamwork skills. Ability to follow established procedures and maintain data integrity. Preferred Qualifications Experience with analytical chemistry techniques such as: HPLC UV-Vis Spectroscopy Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC) Column Chromatography FTIR Titrations Experience in a GMP-regulated laboratory environment. Familiarity with laboratory documentation practices (GMP/GDP). Expe

QC Analyst Job Description The QC Analyst supports both the Quality Control (QC) Lab and the Feed Lab by performing supplemental product testing and feed sample analysis to handle increased sample volumes. This role focuses on wet chemistry, general laboratory testing, and feed analysis while strictly following GMP and GDP guidelines to ensure accurate, reliable data and timely reporting. Responsibilities Perform wet chemistry and general laboratory product testing in the QC Lab, including sieve analysis, thin layer chromatography, and loss on drying using vacuum ovens. Conduct high-throughput testing, completing approximately 12 to 16 tests per day, while managing weighing and sample preparation for materials ranging from 50 mg to 1 g. Accurately document all product testing results in a lab notebook, adhering to GMP and GDP documentation standards. Receive and log feed samples in the Feed Lab, ensuring proper tracking and chain of custody. Carry out sample preparation for feed analysis, including grinding, weighing, and solution preparation. Analyze customer feed samples using HPLC, column chromatography, and UV-Vis techniques in accordance with established procedures. Record feed analysis results following GMP guidelines and report final results to leadership in a clear and timely manner. Manage a typical feed sample load of approximately 16 samples per day, with flexibility to handle increased volumes during busier periods such as late summer. Follow all established procedures, systems, and methods without making unapproved process changes, ensuring consistency and compliance. Collaborate effectively with both a small team in the Feed Lab and a larger QC team, contributing to a positive and cooperative work environment. Learn new methods, instruments, and workflows quickly, applying training to maintain high testing throughput and quality. Maintain laboratory cleanliness and organization, including proper handling of glassware and samples as needed. Essential Skills Hands-on experience with wet chemistry and general laboratory testing techniques. Proficiency in sieve analysis, thin layer chromatography, and loss on drying (LOD) using vacuum ovens. Ability to perform high-throughput testing, managing 12 to 16 tests per day while maintaining accuracy and quality. Strong documentation skills, with the ability to record data in lab notebooks in full compliance with GMP and GDP standards. Experience with feed sample preparation, including grinding, weighing, and solution preparation. Practical experience analyzing samples using HPLC, column chromatography, and UV-Vis. Understanding and application of GMP guidelines in a QC laboratory environment. BS in Chemistry (ACS-accredited degree) with hands-on undergraduate research experience, preferably involving column chromatography, HPLC, or UV-Vis, or up to 6 months of experience in a QC lab (for the first position). This role plays a key part in safeguarding the organization by conducting periodic reassessments, trigger-based reviews, and continuous monitoring of vendor controls across multiple risk domains -including information security, privacy, business continuity, operational resilience, and compliance. Initiate and conduct targeted assessments based on defined cadence and triggers (e.g., breach disclosures, sanctions/adverse media hits, material CVE exposure, breach notifications). Track changes in vendor risk posture and maintain monitoring tiers mapped to inherent risk, data sensitivity, concentration risk, and business criticality. Collaborate with internal subject matter experts (e.g., InfoSec, Privacy, Legal, Compliance, Business Continuity) to validate findings and determine risk impact. Document risk trend analysis and provide clear rationale for any changes in inherent or residual risk ratings.
